summary: A future held at Quote by one client and at Depth by another: the desktop subscribes the depth feed alone while Depth is held (the touchline goes) and both frames carry OI; once Depth is released the touchline comes back and the Quote frame carries no OI.

notes: The desktop subscribes one effective mode per instrument (websocket::manager Entry::effective) and the feeds that mode needs (streaming.rs feeds, mode_change_frames); the web counts references per feed and keeps the touchline for the Quote client. The public frames do not depend on it: the depth feed carries every touchline field.

No frame carries the depth feed's `ltt` (an IST HH:MM:SS): the desktop reads it on the IST day the tick arrives (streaming.rs clock_on_day_of), so its epoch-ms value depends on the day the case runs and cannot be pinned here; brokers::definedge::tests::quote_feed::a_depth_message_carries_the_full_quote_and_the_trade_time pins it. Without it both sides take the feed time `ft` (epoch seconds) as the trade time.

deviations.reason: Definedge's web adapter puts its subscription mode number (1, 2, 3) in data.mode; the desktop sends the label (ltp, quote, full). Lead rule 2026-11-09: data.mode follows the broker's own web adapter, in Phase B through lane wire's per-broker switch in the dialect table (Definedge: integer).

The web forwards Definedge's raw time as ltt: the feed time `ft` in epoch seconds (or the depth feed's clock text HH:MM:SS), a wrong value where feed timestamps are epoch milliseconds (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md); it is a JSON string as well. The desktop sends the epoch ms value.

Definedge's web adapter sends OI as oi only; the desktop adds open_interest beside it. Lead rule 2026-11-09: open_interest follows the broker's own web adapter, in Phase B through lane wire's per-broker switch in the dialect table (Definedge: no open_interest).
The web sends Definedge's percent change (`pc`) for every instrument; the desktop sends the change fields for indices only.
